title: Compile-time policy for dynamic sparsity & expert-routing kernels
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Goal: Produce a deterministic compile-and-publish policy that chooses optimized kernels for models with dynamic sparsity patterns and Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) routing, while enabling model-version pinning and safe rollout.

Background: The runtime currently selects kernels using a set of heuristics derived from static profiles. MoE and GQA models frequently change runtime shapes (active experts per token, group sizes) causing large variance in latency across requests. This ticket defines a compile policy that: (1) collects representative micro-profiles during onboarding, (2) produces a small set of candidate kernel bundles (fast-paths) for the model version, (3) publishes performance profiles to the model catalog, and (4) pins an initial kernel bundle for stable production rollout with canary and automatic rollback hooks.

Scope:
- Onboard flow: sampling and microbenchmark harness for per-layer expert routing distribution and sparsity maps.
- Compiler step: generate 2-4 kernel bundles per model-version covering common routing sparsities and group sizes; emit fingerprints and fallback operators.
- Runtime policy: prefer pinned bundle; if request shape mismatches, attempt compatible bundle (fast checks) then fallback to generic safe-path kernel.
- Catalog: profile entries include median latency, p95, memory high-water, observed expert-count histogram, and compatible bundle IDs.
- Pinning & rollout: APIs to pin model-version -> bundle, canary percent, escalate to broader rollout, automatic rollback on latency or correctness regression.

Acceptance criteria:
1) New onboarding harness produces reproducible microprofiles for MoE/GQA models (test corpus: mix of 3 open-source MoE models).
2) Compiler yields candidate bundles with >=8% median token latency improvement over generic kernel in 90% of cases for at least one bundle.
3) Model catalog stores bundle metadata and supports pinning via console + CLI.
4) Runtime respects pin and performs safe fallback; integration tests validate no correctness regressions on adopted eval prompts.

Trade-offs considered:
- Memory vs latency: specialized kernels reduce execution time but increase binary/code cache size. We limit to 4 bundles to bound memory.
- Compilation time: aggressive per-model compile increases onboarding latency; introduce async background compilation for non-blocking onboarding.
- Telemetry volume: collecting per-token expert histograms increases telemetry cost; downsample to 1% of requests by default and sample 100 sessions per model for onboarding runs.

Rollout plan:
- Phase 1 (dev): enable for internal MoE test models, compile bundles on dev cluster, validate.
- Phase 2 (staged): export profiles to catalog, enable pin UI, run 5% canary traffic for 48h with observability dashboards.
- Phase 3 (prod): enable automatic rollout to pinned bundle after 72h stable signals, expose opt-out to customers.

Observability & SLOs: publish per-bundle latency and correctness metrics to runtime-1.19 dashboard. Add alert rules for delta p95 > 15% or error-rate increase > 0.5%.
